A1.justification: The PDFs describe the same work, renamed from IGSM to 2ndMatch, and their readable main texts, equations, tables, and figures support comparison. However, v1 includes Appendices A–G, while v2 ends after its references despite citing supplementary Sections A.3 and C. Retention or revision of appendix-only material cannot be established.

before.justification: v1 reports original diffusion-model finetuning results, component and pruning-ratio ablations, loss-weight sweeps, training-cost measurements, and OTD projection experiments.

after.justification: v2 retains original finetuning results and adds ImageNet and MSCOCO evaluations, FTLE measurements, and experiments across multiple pruning methods.

M1.justification: The three-component framework remains intact. However, Equation 9 revises the written Jacobian penalty from an unsquared difference involving J-transpose v to a squared difference involving Jv, and the computation description changes from VJPs to JVPs. This is a localized formulation revision; inconsistencies within v1 prevent establishing whether the implementation also changed. Renaming and the explicit per-timestep proxy explanation alone are not new components.

E1.justification: v2 retains CIFAR-10, CelebA, and LSUN coverage and adds class-conditional ImageNet generation at 256×256 and text-to-image evaluation on MSCOCO at 512×512. These introduce substantially different conditioning requirements and image domains, rather than merely additional configurations of the existing tasks.

E2.justification: v2 evaluates BK-SDM Base/Small/Tiny variants and adds Random, LAMP, Magnitude, and Taylor pruning comparisons with baseline, KD, and 2ndMatch finetuning in Table 6. O2MKD, previously evaluated on CIFAR-10 and LSUN-Church, disappears from the supplied comparisons. The U-ViT comparator set remains unchanged, and DeepCache remains in the LSUN comparisons.

E3.justification: Evaluation expands beyond FID to rFID, sFID, precision/recall, IS, CLIP, and ablation FTLE measurements. New protocols include 30,000 MSCOCO samples and 25-step Stable Diffusion sampling. v2 specifies A100 inference measurements, whereas v1 Appendix D used a 2080Ti for throughput. The existing 100-step DDPM and 1000-step U-ViT sampling procedures remain.

E4.justification: v2 adds FTLE-based component analysis, robustness across pruning criteria, and per-class ImageNet rFID and qualitative analysis. Existing component-FID and pruning-ratio analyses largely persist. Conversely, v1's main-text loss-weight analysis and appendix weight sweeps, OTD investigation, and training-cost analysis are not reproduced in the supplied v2; their status in the unavailable supplement is unknown.

E5.justification: Neither supplied PDF reports repeated-run counts, experimental seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests for the results. Additional scalar metrics and generated-sample counts in v2 do not constitute uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: Substantial new results include ImageNet FIDs of 10.23 for Diff-Pruning and 5.68 for 2ndMatch, MSCOCO Base FIDs of 15.76 and 13.84, and ablation FTLE values. These are new comparisons, not same-setting improvements over v1. Retained headline FIDs remain unchanged: 11.25/9.68 on LSUN and 4.05/3.35 on U-ViT CIFAR-10/CelebA. Additional metric columns and pruning-method results substantially expand the reported evidence.

T1.justification: The main-text FTLE explanation corrects maximum perturbation amplification from lambda_max to its square root, consistent with v1 Appendix A. Equation 5 gains the squared L2 norm, and Equation 6 corrects the noise-level indexing. These are mathematical corrections rather than a new theoretical framework. v2's referenced supplementary derivation is unavailable, limiting assessment of further theoretical changes.

C1.justification: Both versions claim a general-purpose, architecture-agnostic finetuning framework combining noise prediction, distillation, and FTLE-inspired second-order Jacobian supervision to narrow the dense–pruned quality gap. v1 already states applicability atop any pruning method. The broader experiments and renamed framework support the same central contribution rather than redefine it.

C2.justification: v2 explicitly qualifies the objective as a local per-timestep sensitivity proxy and interprets newly measured FTLE agreement as mechanism evidence. It also interprets the new experiments as supporting broader pruning and text-to-image applicability. The supplied v2 lacks v1's substantive discussion of training overhead, weight sensitivity, and unsuccessful OTD refinement. Its claim of consistent CLIP improvement conflicts with Table 2, where Tiny decreases from 0.2653 to 0.2636.

D1.justification: v1 supplies torch-pruning versions, detailed architectural and training hyperparameters, memory and training-time measurements, and a code-access statement. These disclosures are not reproduced in the supplied v2, which instead references an unavailable supplement. v2 adds checkpoint-source information and specifies A100 inference hardware. This substantially changes available reproducibility information without establishing that the underlying training settings or repository availability changed.

R1.justification: Related work adds sources such as TinyFusion, Q-DiT, RASS, and efficient finetuning/concept suppression, alongside citations supporting new datasets and metrics. The positioning around finetuning rather than pruning, and sensitivity supervision beyond output distillation, remains stable. The BK-SDM bibliographic update corresponds to the architectural-compression work already cited in v1.

P1.justification: Beyond the IGSM-to-2ndMatch rename and author-name edit, the introduction, related work, method explanation, and experimental narrative are extensively rewritten and condensed. Background subsections become compact paragraphs, and the results narrative is reorganized around expanded model families and revised ablations. This is substantial editorial restructuring.

P2.justification: The document switches from single-column to two-column presentation. v2 adds a front-page Stable Diffusion comparison, replaces the conceptual illustration, and introduces an ImageNet chart and sample panel. Tables are substantially redesigned with additional metric columns, split dataset blocks, and new ablation layouts. v1's appendix galleries and tables are not present in the supplied v2.

improvement.justification: ImageNet/MSCOCO evaluations and direct FTLE and pruning-method analyses substantially strengthen empirical support, while corrected equations improve clarity. However, the supplied v2 lacks v1's detailed reproducibility, training-cost, sensitivity, and limitations material, and its uniform CLIP-improvement claim contradicts the Tiny result in Table 2. The unavailable supplement prevents resolving whether important supporting information was preserved. These material benefits and deficiencies do not support a reliable net quality judgment.
